successors.note: On Gian Gastone's death 'Francis Stephen of Lorraine became heir to the Tuscan throne'; the Treaty of Vienna (1738) made Don Carlos give up the succession. Cliopatria's Grand Duchy of Tuscany row starts only in 1797, so 1737-1796 is a gap to be given to that dossier.

keyframe_review.note: 14,118 km2: the 1279 outline plus Pisa, Livorno and seven Greek cells. Florence took Pisa on 9 October 1406 ('took Pisa on 9 October 1406 after a long siege') and bought Livorno on 28 August 1421, so for 1402-1405 the 1384 keyframe applies. The seven cells at about 38.6 N, 22.2 E (Phocis, around Amfissa and Delphi) are not Florentine on any page opened: the Duchy of Athens page gives Athens in 1388-1458 to 'the Acciaioli family of Florence', a family, not the Republic.

correction.text: the 1407 outline without its Greek cells; years 1406-1486 (to be read with Pisa from October 1406 and Livorno from August 1421)

keyframe_review.note: 14,167 km2 including 7 Greek cells, which the Duchy of Athens page does not give to the Republic ('The Florentine Acciaioli governed the duchy'; Ottoman conquest 1456 or 1458). The shape holds from October 1406 without the Greek cells; Livorno joins on 28 August 1421 (its two cells are in the shape from 1407, a 14-year early start).

12,065 km2: the Greek cells gone (the Greek part was never the Republic's, see 1407). Piero de' Medici was forced to give up Pisa and Livorno in late 1494 and the page says Pisa was 'de facto independent' afterwards, so this outline holds 1487-1493 only.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1494-1508: Florence without Pisa, which revolted during the French passage. The page says Piero de' Medici gave up 'the fortresses of Sarzanello, Sarzana and Pietrasanta' and 'Pisa and Livorno, with their ports'; the Florence page says Pisa 'had been de facto independent since' Charles VIII's invasion. When Florence regained Pisa is not on any page opened (1509 is the researcher's bridging).
12,041 km2: the same outline, 24 km2 smaller than 1487 (a Forli fringe). It holds from 1509, when Pisa is back, to 1547.

12,539 km2: the 1507 outline plus Elba. 'Florence purchased the island of Elba from the Republic of Genoa (in 1548)', a year after Cliopatria's start. The shape holds 1548-1556: Siena's territory was occupied in April 1555 but legally Florence's only from July 1557 (ledger occupation).

20,111 km2, the same outline. The page gives 1852 infobox area 21,710 km2 for the later grand duchy (ratio 1.09 against the 1734 shape of 19,853 km2), within the factor of two; the 1852 figure includes lands added after 1815.

region.text: the commune and its immediate contado

ledger.note: 1115: the commune of Florence is established. 'The republic originated in 1115' (infobox 'First established: 1115'). The page gives no extent; a disc around the city stands in.

1254: Pistoia in Florence's succession table. The page's table lists 'Pistoia (1254)' with no narrative; Cliopatria's 1260 outline already contains Pistoia. A later subjection to Florence is not on the page.
1361: Volterra joins Florence. The succession table lists 'Volterra (1361)'; the page gives no narrative. Cliopatria's 1260 outline includes the district.

1384: Arezzo yields to Florence. 'It functioned as an independent city-state until 1384'; 'yielded to Florentine domination in 1384'; the Florence page's table gives 'Arezzo (1384)'. The page does not say how (purchase or conquest).

1406: Florence takes Pisa. Maso degli Albizzi 'took Pisa on 9 October 1406 after a long siege'; the Pisa page says it was occupied by the mercenaries Angelo Tartaglia and Muzio Attendolo Sforza, who ordered annexation to Florence; Gabriele Maria Visconti is its ruler 1402-1406.

1421: Florence buys Livorno from Genoa. 'on 28 August 1421 it was bought by the Republic of Florence' at 'the price of 100.000 Tuscan florin'; Pisa had sold it to the Visconti in 1399 and Milan to Genoa in 1405.

1494: Piero de' Medici gives Pisa and Livorno to Charles VIII and Pisa breaks away. Piero 'was forced to grant him the fortresses of Sarzanello, Sarzana and Pietrasanta' and gave up 'Pisa and Livorno, with their ports' (late October to early November 1494); he fled on 8-9 November. The Florence page: Pisa 'had been de facto independent since' Charles's invasion. The pages do not say Pisa revolted; the Cliopatria shape draws Pisa as Florentine throughout.

1509: Florence regains Pisa. The Republic of Florence page: 'the Secretary of War, Niccolò Machiavelli, recaptured Pisa in 1509', Pisa having 'been de facto independent since Charles VIII's invasion'. No month on the page. (Reviewer eu-13-i: the year is on the cited page; confidence raised from 1.)

1532: the republic becomes the hereditary Duchy of Florence under Alessandro de' Medici. The page's infobox gives 'Duchy of Florence: 1532' and the text that in April 1532 the constitution 'formally created a hereditary monarchy'; the Grand Duchy page dates the enactment to 27 April and Charles V's creation of the Medici as hereditary rulers to 12 August 1530. Colour and dossier continue.
1548: Florence buys Elba. 'Florence purchased the island of Elba from the Republic of Genoa (in 1548).' The page gives no month; Cliopatria's shape has Elba from 1547.

region.text: Montalcino, seat of the exiled government of Siena

ledger.note: 1555: the exiled government of Siena holds Montalcino. The Montalcino government 'did not concede defeat in the Battle of Marciano and continued to resist Tuscan rule until 1559'. The page gives no month; the siege of Siena ended in April 1555.

region.text: Siena's territory: the 1556 shape without the 1547 shape; the page gives about 8,000 km2

ledger.note: 1555: Siena falls to Florence and Spain. 'On 17 April 1555, Florence and Spain occupied the territory of Siena'; the Siena page says 'Siena surrendered to Spain on 21 April 1555, marking the end of the Republic'. The two pages differ by four days; the territory is the occupation until Philip II's grant.

region.text: Siena's territory: the 1556 shape without the 1547 shape; the page gives about 8,000 km2

ledger.note: 1557: Philip II hands Siena to Cosimo. In July 1557 Philip II 'bestowed on Cosimo as a hereditary fiefdom'; the Siena page: he 'ceded Siena's entire territory to the Duchy of Florence' (no date), excluding 'a series of coastal fortress annexed to the State of the Presidi'.

region.text: Siena's territory: the 1556 shape without the 1547 shape; the page gives about 8,000 km2

ledger.note: 1557: Cosimo I of Florence receives the Sienese state as a hereditary fief. Cliopatria draws it as Florentine from 1556; the Grand Duchy page has 'Cosimo conquered Siena (in 1555)' and gives no 1557 date.

region.text: Montalcino, seat of the exiled government of Siena

ledger.note: 1559: Tuscan troops annex Montalcino. 'Tuscan troops arrived and annexed Montalcino, too' (1559); the last of the Sienese state is gone.

region.text: Montalcino, seat of the exiled government of Siena

ledger.note: 1559: Montalcino joins the Florentine duchy. 'Tuscan troops arrived and annexed Montalcino, too'; the page gives no month.

1569: Cosimo I becomes Grand Duke of Tuscany. 'was elevated by a papal bull of Pope Pius V to Grand Duke of Tuscany on 27 August 1569'; the Republic page: this 'marks the end of the Florence Republic'. Imperial confirmation by Maximilian followed in 1575 and Philip II's recognition in 1576. Colour and dossier continue.

1737: the Medici line ends with Gian Gastone. 'On 9 July 1737, Gian Gastone died; the last male Medici of the grand ducal line'; 'Soon after, Francis Stephen of Lorraine became heir to the Tuscan throne' and Don Carlos 'was forced to give up the Tuscan succession by the Treaty of Vienna (1738)'. The History page: the extinction of the Medici line and the accession in 1737 of Francis Stephen brought Tuscany under the Austrian crown.

wars.name: Florentine conquest of Pisa
wars.outcome: Maso degli Albizzi took Pisa on 9 October 1406 after a long siege and the city was annexed to Florence.
wars.note: The Pisa page says the mercenaries Angelo Tartaglia and Muzio Attendolo Sforza occupied the city and ordered the annexation; neither page gives a 1405 start.

wars.name: Italian War of 1494-1495

zones.text: Pisa and Livorno, given up to Charles VIII

wars.outcome: Piero de' Medici surrendered Sarzanello, Sarzana, Pietrasanta, Pisa and Livorno, was driven out on 8-9 November 1494 and the republic was restored; Charles VIII's occupation of Florence ended when he left for Rome in late November 1494.
wars.note: The page does not mention a Pisan revolt; whether Livorno stayed in French hands is not on any page.

wars.name: Pisan rebellion against Florence
wars.outcome: Pisa was 'de facto independent' from the French invasion of 1494 and was regained by Florence.
wars.note: The end year 1509 is not on any page opened (conf 1 in the ledger).

wars.name: Siege of Florence
wars.outcome: The Medici were restored after a protracted siege; Charles V created them hereditary rulers on 12 August 1530 and the republic became the Duchy of Florence in 1532.
wars.note: The History page: 'a Spanish siege ended the Republic of Florence'. No border moved.

wars.name: War of Siena

zones.text: Siena's territory: the 1556 shape without the 1547 shape; the page gives about 8,000 km2
Montalcino, seat of the exiled government of Siena

wars.outcome: The Sienese expelled the Spanish garrison in 1552 and allied with France; Piero Strozzi was beaten at Marciano in August 1554; Siena surrendered on 21 April 1555; Philip II ceded the territory to Cosimo in July 1557 and Tuscan troops annexed Montalcino in 1559.
wars.note: Page title of the war not opened. The Florence page has 17 April 1555 for the occupation, the Siena page 21 April for the surrender.

certainty.note: No page opened gives survey or treaty lines for Florence; the outlines are Cliopatria's approximations, corrected only where a page dates an acquisition. Elba and Siena's territory are the best-known edges.

notes: Pages opened: 9 of the up to 9 budgeted. The Italian War of 1499-1504 and Italian War of 1494-1498 titles did not load; the 1494-1495 article (found by search) was used instead. Cliopatria rows to correct: (1) no shape before 1260 although the page dates the commune to 1115; (2) the constant 1260-1401 outline already contains Arezzo (annexed 1384) and fringes of Pisa, Siena and Bologna, so it describes the late 14th-century contado; (3) the 1402-1486 shapes carry seven Greek cells at about 38.6 N, 22.2 E (Phocis) that no page ties to the Republic (the Acciaioli of Athens were a Florentine family; the Cliopatria Duchy of Athens row stops in 1313, so Athens 1388-1458 is a gap for the Greece group); (4) Pisa's independence 1494-1509 is not drawn; (5) Siena is Florentine in Cliopatria from 1556 although the legal grant is July 1557 (occupation recorded for 1555-1557). The row is one state with two renames (Duchy of Florence 1532, Grand Duchy of Tuscany 1569) and ends with the Medici in 1737; the Lorraine Grand Duchy 1737-1796 has no Cliopatria shape (Cliopatria's Grand Duchy of Tuscany starts 1797) and should extend the grand-duchy-of-tuscany dossier. Page silent: Montaperti (1260), Campaldino (1289), the dates of Prato, Colle, San Gimignano, Montepulciano, Cortona (1411) and Pietrasanta; Pisa's 1494 revolt and 1509 reconquest; the Siena grant of July 1557 comes from the Florence page only; Montalcino month. Dates disagree: Siena occupied 17 April 1555 (Florence page) against surrendered 21 April 1555 (Siena page). Needs dossiers: republic-of-siena, Republic of Siena in Montalcino (1555-1559), second-republic-of-pisa (1494-1509), the Acciaioli Duchy of Athens (1388-1458), the Commune of Arezzo, and the early Tuscan communes. No ruler strip: the pages do not give a complete list.
